prompt: A fintech startup has 50 developers who deploy more than 40 microservices every week. Each service needs a dedicated IAM role, so role requests occur several times a day. Currently, the security team creates the roles on behalf of the developers, and deployments are frequently blocked while waiting for approval. The platform team wants to delegate to developers the ability to create IAM roles for their services on their own. However, the platform team must prevent developers from escalating their privileges by creating roles that have administrator permissions. Developers must be able to create roles immediately without waiting for approval. The security team has only 3 members and cannot rely on after-the-fact reviews or manual attachment. The developer accounts are consolidated in a single organization, and most service roles need access only to Amazon S3, Amazon SQS, and Amazon DynamoDB. The last audit flagged a large number of exception approvals. Which configuration will meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Grant developers the iam:* permission. Use an SCP to deny only the action of attaching the AdministratorAccess managed policy to a role, to block the escalation path.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When a developer creates a role, use an AWS Config rule to detect roles that have no boundary policy. Have the security team manually attach a boundary policy the next day.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the developer policy, allow iam:CreateRole and iam:AttachRolePolicy only if a specified permissions boundary policy is attached. Deny modification and deletion of the boundary policy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Accept role creation requests as tickets. Have the security team create the roles on behalf of developers, and grant developers only the iam:PassRole permission.

explanation: By using the iam:PermissionsBoundary condition key to allow role creation and policy attachment only when the specified boundary policy is attached, every role that is created is restricted within the boundary. Modification and deletion of the boundary policy must also be denied so that it cannot be bypassed. This approach allows immediate creation and requires no human involvement. An SCP that denies only iam:* and attachment of the administrator policy can be bypassed with other broad policies or inline policies. Manual attachment after the fact leaves the roles exposed without a boundary in the meantime. The ticket-based approach violates the requirement for immediate creation.

prompt: A retail company's AWS organization consists of 120 accounts across 3 Regions, and each account administrator changes security groups frequently. Last quarter, there was an incident in which a development account left port 22 open to 0.0.0.0/0 for two weeks. The security team has only 4 members and cannot inspect every account. From now on, the company must detect the creation of such a rule within minutes and automatically revert it with no human involvement. The history of rule changes must be retained for auditing, and maintaining separate scripts for each account is not allowed. Different teams operate each Region, so once a rule is defined, it must be applied in the same way to new accounts and new Regions. The evaluation results for noncompliant resources must be viewable aggregated at the organization level. Which configuration will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy the restricted-ssh AWS Config managed rule as an organization conformance pack, and attach an AWS Systems Manager Automation automatic remediation action for violations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Export the AWS Trusted Advisor security group check results every week for the security team to review, and open a ticket for the responsible account administrator to fix each violation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receive Amazon Inspector network reachability findings through Amazon EventBridge, and implement an AWS Lambda function that deletes the violating security group rules one account at a time.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a custom AWS Config rule that runs every 24 hours in every account, review the results on a dashboard, and have the responsible person fix the rules directly in the console.

explanation: restricted-ssh is a managed rule whose evaluation is triggered when a security group configuration changes, so it finds violations within minutes. Attaching a Systems Manager Automation runbook as an automatic remediation action reverts the change with no human involvement. An organization conformance pack deploys the rule and the remediation action to all accounts with the same configuration from a single template, and the evaluation history is also retained in AWS Config. A weekly Trusted Advisor review violates both the within-minutes requirement and the automatic reversion requirement. Inspector reachability applies to EC2 targets and requires you to implement Lambda directly. A 24-hour evaluation cycle with manual fixes leaves delay and human involvement.

prompt: A banking-affiliated fintech company protects customer data with SSE-KMS in Amazon S3. The financial regulator requires that key material exist only in HSMs in the company's data center and that all encryption and decryption operations also be performed in those HSMs. The company already has redundant on-premises HSMs and a team that operates them. If the company revokes access, ciphertext remaining in AWS must be impossible to decrypt. Importing key material and using HSMs inside AWS are not allowed, and storing key material in any other way is considered a regulatory violation. The ciphertext is stored in Amazon S3. The regulator conducts an inspection every six months to verify proof of key ownership, and all S3 buckets used by the application are in the Seoul Region. Which AWS KMS configuration will meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Connect an external key store (XKS) to the on-premises external key manager through an XKS proxy that the company operates, and create the KMS key inside that external key store.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure an AWS CloudHSM cluster in a VPC, create a CloudHSM key store, and have the key material and operations for the KMS key performed in dedicated HSMs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a customer managed KMS key, and use the key policy to allow only the Amazon S3 service principal to use it, keeping key usage under the company's control.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an external-origin (EXTERNAL) KMS key by importing key material generated in the on-premises HSM, and set a short expiration time for the key material.

explanation: The correct answer is an external key store. With XKS, an external key manager owned by the company stores the key material and performs encryption and decryption. If access is revoked, AWS cannot access the key and therefore cannot decrypt the ciphertext. In exchange, responsibility for availability, latency, and durability shifts to the customer. Importing key material copies the key material to AWS HSMs and the operations also occur in AWS, and this approach is prohibited. A CloudHSM key store has its HSMs inside AWS and so does not satisfy the on-premises storage requirement. Restricting the key policy does not change the fact that the key material is in an AWS HSM.

prompt: A financial company manages 28 AWS Config rules that implement its internal security standards, together with AWS Systems Manager Automation remediation actions to run on noncompliance, as a single bundle. Some of these are custom rules written directly by the company's security team. Currently, every time a new account is created, an administrator creates the rules by hand, so the settings differ slightly from account to account. The company wants to deploy this bundle consistently to the 90 member accounts of the organization and to make changes in only one place. The target Regions are Seoul and Tokyo, and the security team has 5 members. Changes occur about once per quarter, and every change must be completed in a single approved deployment. The audit team wants to see at a glance which accounts are using which version of the bundle. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable the AWS Control Tower mandatory controls on all OUs so that the organization applies, in bulk, the rules that correspond to the internal standards.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard in AWS Security Hub across the organization to check accounts against the same standard and automatically remediate violations.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Log in to each member account, create the 28 Config rules one by one in the console, attach a remediation action to each rule, and distribute the procedure as a document.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the management account or a delegated administrator account, define the rules and remediation actions in a YAML template and deploy them to all member accounts as an organization conformance pack.

explanation: The correct answer is an organization conformance pack. A conformance pack bundles AWS Config managed or custom rules and remediation actions in a single YAML template, deploys them as a single unit to a single account and Region or to an entire organization, and lets you modify them in one place. Creating rules manually per account requires repeating 28 rules across 90 accounts and breaks consistency. The FSBP standard is a set of controls defined by AWS and cannot contain the company's own rules and specified remediation actions. Control Tower mandatory controls are also protective controls defined by AWS and cannot be used as a bundle of custom company rules.

prompt: A VPC that runs 300 Amazon EC2 instances for a payment workload was recently assessed as having a high likelihood of a security incident. The company must block the instances in the VPC from resolving known malicious domains. In addition, a path has been identified in which some instances bypass the VPC resolver and query public DNS servers on the internet directly (port 53), and this path must also be blocked. Amazon Route 53 Resolver query logging and Amazon GuardDuty are already enabled, but an approach that only detects does not meet the requirements. All instances are in private subnets, and the security groups already restrict destination ports, but outbound port 53 is open. Resolution of internal names for normal services must continue to be handled by the VPC resolver. Which TWO actions will meet these two requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Send Route 53 Resolver query logs to Amazon S3, periodically query for malicious domain lookups with Amazon Athena, and deliver a report to the responsible person.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add a stateful rule to AWS Network Firewall that drops TCP and UDP port 53 traffic leaving the VPC, and make the outbound path go through the firewall.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receive GuardDuty DNS-related findings through Amazon EventBridge, and automate an AWS Lambda function to isolate, after the fact, the instances that queried a malicious domain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a rule that blocks the AWS managed malicious domain list to a Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall rule group, and associate the rule group with the VPC.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Apply AWS Shield Advanced to the VPC and configure it to automatically mitigate abnormal query traffic destined for public DNS servers.

explanation: DNS Firewall blocks queries that pass through the VPC resolver based on domain lists, but it cannot see queries that bypass the resolver and go directly to an external DNS server. Network Firewall blocks that path by dropping external port 53 traffic, so both actions must be used together to meet the requirements. Automatic isolation based on GuardDuty is a response after the fact, after the query has already gone out. Query logging and Athena lookups provide visibility only and cannot block. Shield Advanced is a DDoS protection service and is unrelated to domain blocking.

prompt: CloudTrail confirms signs that temporary credentials for the IAM role PaymentProcessorRole, used by an e-commerce company's payment service, were leaked through malware on a developer's laptop. The role has a maximum session duration of 12 hours and hundreds of active sessions, and because it is the middle of a Black Friday event, payment processing cannot be stopped for long. Normal workloads must resume immediately by obtaining new credentials with the same role ARN, and deleting the role or modifying the content of the existing permissions policies is not allowed. It is not possible to identify individually which session the leaked credentials belong to, and although the laptop has been isolated, an attacker can access payment data for as long as the already-issued credentials remain valid. Which action will immediately invalidate the already-issued credentials?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Temporarily attach an SCP that denies all actions to the organization root so that all principals in the account are prevented from sending new requests.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delete the role, re-create it with the same name, and replicate the trust policy and permissions policy so that the existing credentials are no longer valid.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduce the maximum session duration of the role from 12 hours to 1 hour so that credentials issued from now on expire within a short time.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run revoke active sessions for the role in the IAM console so that requests made with credentials issued before this moment are all denied.

explanation: The correct answer is revoking the role's active sessions. This feature adds an AWSRevokeOlderSessions deny inline policy to the role, which denies all credentials issued up to the revocation time (about 30 seconds later, allowing for propagation delay). It does not apply to sessions assumed afterward, so normal workloads resume by obtaining new credentials with the same role ARN. The content of the existing permissions policies is not changed. Deleting and re-creating the role violates the constraint that prohibits deletion, and the role's unique ID changes, which can break references. Reducing the maximum session duration changes only the lifetime of sessions issued in the future and does not invalidate already-leaked credentials. Denying all actions with a root SCP also blocks workloads unrelated to this role and the resumption of normal operations, so it does not fit the requirements.

prompt: A healthcare data company has an Amazon S3 bucket containing approximately 10 TB of patient consultation records, and it must check for personal information every quarter. The bucket is encrypted with a customer managed KMS key (SSE-KMS), and the key and the bucket are owned by the same account. When an Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery job was run, many objects were reported with metadata only and without content analysis, and almost no sensitive data findings were produced. There is no problem with the bucket policy, the sampling depth is 100%, and the security team has one week left before this quarter's inspection deadline. The discovery job must not affect other teams' buckets in the account, and the security administrator can modify the key policy directly. Because the same bucket is scanned again every quarter, the fix must continue to work afterward once it is applied. Which action will allow Macie to analyze the object content?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a statement to the bucket policy that allows the Macie service-linked role to perform s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket, to open up object read permissions first.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower the object sampling depth of the discovery job, and instead adjust the job scope to be split by object prefix and run in multiple separate runs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the bucket default encryption to SSE-C, and modify the application to pass a customer-provided key in the request header for every newly uploaded object.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a statement to the KMS key policy that allows the Macie service-linked role AWSServiceRoleForAmazonMacie to perform kms:Decrypt.

explanation: Macie decrypts and analyzes objects encrypted with a customer managed key only when the key policy allows the service-linked role to perform kms:Decrypt. If it is not allowed, Macie stores and reports only metadata. When the same account owns the key and the bucket, adding a statement to the key policy is sufficient. Adjusting the bucket policy is unrelated to the cause because the problem statement says there is no problem with it. The sampling depth is already 100%, so there is nothing more to change. Objects encrypted with SSE-C cannot be decrypted by Macie, so this would make analysis impossible instead.

prompt: A logistics company must apply customer managed KMS key encryption to its unencrypted production Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database (Multi-AZ, 1.5 TB). The service runs 24 hours a day, and orders are lost if write traffic is interrupted, so the write downtime during the transition must be kept as short as possible. Data loss is not allowed, and changes to the application's endpoint settings must be minimal. The transition will be performed during the nighttime maintenance window, and a plan to return to the previous state if a problem occurs must also be in place. Five reporting tools connected to the same database have hardcoded the endpoint and are difficult to change. The storage is gp3, and order processing stops if write latency exceeds a certain level. Before the switchover, the company must verify that all storage data in the new environment has been loaded and that latency has stabilized. Which method is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a read replica from the unencrypted instance that is encrypted with a customer managed key, and promote the replica when the replication lag disappears.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When creating a blue/green deployment, specify a customer managed key as the target KMS key for the green DB instance to create an encrypted green environment, and switch over after synchronization and storage loading are complete.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Modify the running DB instance to turn on the storage encryption option, specify a customer managed key, and apply immediately with an instance reboot.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a manual snapshot, copy it while encrypting it with a customer managed key, restore a new instance from the copy, and move the application to the new endpoint.

explanation: The correct answer is encrypting the green environment of a blue/green deployment with a customer managed key. When you create a blue/green deployment, you can encrypt the green instance with a different KMS key by using TargetKmsKeyId in the target resource configuration, and this is documented as a way to encrypt an unencrypted instance. At switchover, RDS renames the green instance to the same name and endpoint as blue, so the hardcoded endpoints do not need to be changed. Because the switchover happens after synchronization catches up, the write downtime is short. If the switchover fails, the changes are rolled back and the previous blue instance also remains. The green instance is restored from a snapshot and then lazily loaded, so completing storage initialization before the switchover stabilizes latency. An instance can be encrypted only at creation, so you cannot turn on encryption by modifying an existing instance. An encrypted read replica of an unencrypted instance cannot be created. Copying and restoring a snapshot is possible, but writes made after the snapshot must be applied separately and the endpoint must be changed, so the downtime is longer.

prompt: A company that operates a global service runs an Amazon Aurora global database in Seoul (primary) and Tokyo (secondary), and applications in both Regions read the same database credentials from AWS Secrets Manager. Security policy requires that the password be rotated automatically every 30 days and that the values in both Regions always match. Applications in Tokyo must be able to read the secret even during a Seoul Region outage. The operations team has 3 members and wants to avoid the burden of configuring and checking a rotation function separately for each Region. The Tokyo application normally reads the secret through the local Region endpoint to reduce latency, and redeploying the applications in both Regions when the database password changes is not allowed. At rotation, the applications in both Regions must see the same value. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule and an AWS Lambda function to copy the value to AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store in the Tokyo Region whenever the Seoul secret changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have the Tokyo application call the Secrets Manager endpoint in the Seoul Region directly, and do not create a separate secret in Tokyo.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create independent secrets in Seoul and Tokyo, and configure a rotation Lambda function for each secret so that the database password is rotated every 30 days.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure automatic rotation only on the primary secret in Seoul and replicate it to the Tokyo Region, so that the Tokyo replica is encrypted with a KMS key in the Tokyo Region.

explanation: The correct answer is to configure rotation on the primary secret and replicate it to Tokyo. When the primary secret is rotated, the new value is propagated to all replicas, so there is no need to manage rotation for each replica, and the replica can be encrypted with a key in the Tokyo Region, so it can be read from Tokyo even during a Seoul outage. Rotating two independent secrets separately would change the same database password twice independently and cause the values to diverge. Copying to Parameter Store would require a heavy burden of direct implementation. Calling the Seoul endpoint cannot read the secret during a Seoul outage.

prompt: A media service with users around the world operates an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses an internet-facing ALB as its origin, and AWS WAF is associated with CloudFront. The ALB security group currently allows port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. However, an attacker has discovered the ALB's DNS name and is connecting to it directly, bypassing CloudFront, where WAF is associated. The solution must not increase the maintenance burden of people continually updating security group rules, and the user response path must remain the same as it is now. Traffic averages tens of millions of requests per day, and origin response time must not increase. The security team wants to block the path by which requests that do not go through CloudFront reach the origin, at both L3/L4 and L7. Which TWO actions will ensure that the ALB accepts only requests that come through CloudFront? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Download the public IP ranges of the CloudFront edge servers directly, register them as ALB security group rules, and update them manually whenever the ranges change.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change the ALB security group inbound rules to allow only port 443 traffic from the AWS managed prefix list for CloudFront origin-facing servers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replace the ALB listener certificate with an ACM public certificate and upgrade the TLS security policy to the latest version to block clients that connect directly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Have CloudFront add a custom header with a secret value to origin requests, and configure the ALB listener rule to forward only requests that have that header and return 403 for all others.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Use Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to steer users toward CloudFront, and do not publicly disclose the ALB's DNS name.

explanation: The managed prefix list is updated by AWS even if the CloudFront origin-facing IPs change, so it blocks direct access at L3/L4 without any security group maintenance burden. The secret custom header lets the ALB listener rule forward only requests that came through CloudFront at L7. Managing the edge IP ranges directly keeps adding update work. Changing the certificate and TLS policy does not restrict the access path. Steering with DNS routing cannot stop an attacker who already knows the ALB DNS name from connecting directly.

prompt: The AWS Security Hub CSPM findings that analysts on a large enterprise's security operations team review each day average 600, and most are low-risk items from development environments. Informational-level findings are piling up from 30 accounts in the organization's development OU, and analysts are missing findings from production accounts. Findings for the same controls in production accounts must continue to be displayed as they are now, and the company wants to avoid disabling controls or writing and operating code. The security team has 4 members, and the administrator account is already delegated. Findings from development accounts must not be deleted entirely and must be retrievable when needed, and suppressed findings must not appear on the analysts' default dashboard. Which solution has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disable the relevant controls in all accounts across the organization and re-enable them only in production accounts, to stop findings from being generated in development accounts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the administrator account, create an automation rule that uses the development account IDs and informational severity as conditions and changes the workflow status to SUPPRESSED.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Write and deploy a function so that an Amazon EventBridge rule and AWS Lambda call BatchUpdateFindings to change the status whenever a development account finding is received.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a custom insight filtered by the development account IDs, and change the work procedure so that analysts view only the insight instead of the default findings screen.

explanation: An automation rule is defined in the administrator account with conditions such as account ID and severity, automatically changes attributes such as the workflow status when findings are ingested, and requires no code. Disabling controls stops the generation of findings, so there is a risk of affecting production accounts as well, and it is not the method requested. Lambda and BatchUpdateFindings create the burden of writing and operating code. An insight only filters the view and cannot change the status of findings, so development findings keep piling up. Also note that a rule applies to findings ingested after it is created.

prompt: A data processing platform uses KMS CreateGrant just before a job starts to give the batch worker role in the same account the Decrypt permission on a specific key, and revokes the grant when the job finishes. This approach comes from a security design that grants only temporary permissions per job, and thousands of jobs run every day. The key policy cannot be modified each time because of the change approval process. However, the first Decrypt call immediately after a grant is created intermittently fails with AccessDenied, and the job is retried. The grant applies to only one specific key, and the permission must disappear as soon as the job ends. Lengthening the retry logic was not accepted because of job delays. Which method guarantees use immediately after the grant is created while minimizing code changes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a kms:Decrypt allow for the worker role to the key policy as a permanent statement so that access is possible without a grant.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add kms:* permissions on the key to the worker role's IAM policy so that all KMS operations are allowed regardless of the grant propagation delay.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pass the grant token returned by CreateGrant in the GrantTokens parameter of the first Decrypt request so that the grant can be used before it propagates.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use ListGrants to look up the ID of the grant that was just created, and call Decrypt passing that grant ID as the GrantTokens value.

explanation: The correct answer is to pass the grant token. KMS uses an eventual consistency model, so AccessDenied can occur immediately after a grant is created and before propagation completes. If you include the grant token returned by CreateGrant in the request, you can use the grant's permissions immediately, even before propagation. Adding a permanent allow to the key policy violates the change process constraint and also defeats the purpose of temporary permissions. Giving kms:* in the IAM policy grants excessive permissions and does not solve the problem if the key policy does not allow it. ListGrants returns only the grant ID and not the token, and the token can be obtained only from CreateGrant.

prompt: A cloud security team has an internal standard that EBS snapshots must not be shareable publicly from any account. Until now, the team has used an SCP that denies ec2:ModifySnapshotAttribute, but the team needs a guarantee that the standard will continue to hold even when the service adds new APIs or features. Account administrators already hold many IAM policies that include snapshot sharing permissions, so it is difficult to revoke the policies in bulk. The scope is 150 accounts, and the security team wants to enforce this standard without depending on the cooperation of account administrators. In the past, the security team had to modify the SCP every time a new API was added, and as a result the standard was left unenforced for two weeks on one occasion. Which method will apply the standard consistently across the 150 accounts?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy to the organization a configuration that uses an AWS Config rule to detect snapshots that can be publicly restored and uses AWS Lambda automatic remediation to remove the sharing setting.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In AWS Organizations, specify block public access for snapshots as blocked in an EC2 declarative policy, and attach it to the organization root.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add more EC2 API names related to snapshot sharing to the SCP to expand the deny list, and update the policy every time a new API is released.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Distribute guidance for account administrators to turn on EBS snapshot block public access on their own, and verify whether it is set by using CloudTrail logs.

explanation: The correct answer is an EC2 declarative policy. A declarative policy enforces the desired configuration directly at the service control plane, so the standard persists even when the service adds new features or APIs, and it supports the Snapshot Block Public Access attribute. SCPs control permissions at the API level, so the deny list must be updated whenever a new API appears, which does not meet the requirement for a lasting guarantee. Detection and automatic remediation with AWS Config are a reactive response that fixes the problem after the snapshot becomes public, leaving a window of exposure. Manual per-account settings cannot guarantee consistency or enforcement.

prompt: The legal team requires both disk evidence and memory evidence from an EBS-backed Amazon EC2 instance suspected of being compromised. Traffic has already been drained from this instance in the production service, volatile data must not be lost, and the evidence collection process must be recorded. The collected evidence is stored in encrypted buckets and snapshots in a dedicated incident response account. The suspect instance is a single m5.2xlarge with 3 EBS volumes attached. The incident response account is in a separate security OU of the organization, and there are two forensic analysts. Every evidence collection step must be traceable to who did what and when, and the analysts can access the instance through SSM Agent. Which TWO actions are MOST appropriate to secure both kinds of evidence without stopping or terminating the instance? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run a read-only memory acquisition tool on the running instance, save the memory image to the evidence bucket, and record its hash.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Install an antivirus agent on the instance to clean up malicious files, then create a snapshot to keep evidence of the clean state, and return the instance to service.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stop the instance first, then create snapshots of the attached EBS volumes to freeze the disk state, and perform later analysis from the snapshots.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Without stopping the instance, create snapshots of all attached EBS volumes, share them with the incident response account, and keep encrypted copies there.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Terminate the instance with the delete-on-termination option turned off so that the EBS volumes remain, and attach them to another instance later for investigation.

explanation: Volatile data such as memory and processes is lost when an instance is stopped, terminated, or rebooted, and EBS snapshots contain only the data written to the volume, so memory must be acquired separately. Therefore, two actions together preserve both kinds of evidence: first acquiring a memory image with a read-only tool while the instance remains running and recording its hash, and then creating snapshots of all volumes without stopping the instance and moving them to the incident response account. Stopping first and then taking snapshots preserves the disk but loses the memory evidence. Terminating and preserving only the volumes also loses the memory. Cleaning files with antivirus alters files and timestamps, which destroys evidence and also breaks the chain of custody.

prompt: A video streaming company protects its Amazon CloudFront distributions and ALB with AWS Shield Advanced and subscribes to Business Support. After an outage caused by a surge of web requests last quarter, the company wants to set up a system in which the AWS Shield Response Team (SRT) contacts the company first when an event occurs. The company has registered the protected resources and two SRT contacts, has enabled the proactive engagement feature, and has created the web ACLs with AWS WAF v2. However, the SRT did not contact the company first even in a recent web request surge incident. The operations team has 3 members, and the company does not want to upgrade the support plan because of cost. The SRT contacts have both an email address and a phone number registered, and the Shield Advanced subscription is under consolidated billing for the entire organization. Which action will make proactive engagement work?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the subscription tier by upgrading the support plan from Business to Enterprise, because that is the only way to meet the SRT proactive engagement requirement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable the Shield Advanced cost protection feature to meet the conditions for being reimbursed for usage charges that increased because of a DDoS attack, and then start the SRT contact procedure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Associate Route 53 health checks with each protected resource and configure the health checks to reflect the actual application health.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Re-create the web ACLs with AWS WAF Classic and change the configuration to pre-delegate permissions that let the SRT modify rules directly.

explanation: SRT proactive engagement determines whether an event qualifies for proactive engagement by looking at the status of the Route 53 health check associated with the protected resource. Without a health check, the SRT does not contact you first even if it detects the event. A Business or Enterprise Support plan satisfies the requirement, so no tier change is needed. Cost protection addresses charge increases caused by DDoS and is separate from proactive engagement. The web ACL must be AWS WAF v2, so reverting to Classic would actually violate the requirement.

prompt: A global fintech company stores customer documents encrypted with the AWS Encryption SDK in Amazon S3 in the Seoul Region, and it must also decrypt the same documents in the Tokyo Region, its disaster recovery Region. Decryption must be possible even during a Seoul Region outage, and the data must not be re-encrypted and the KMS in the Seoul Region must not be called. The company wants to control key policies separately for each Region. Even during normal operation, the company wants decryption to complete within each Region without cross-Region calls, and the ciphertext has already been copied to both Regions. Security policy requires that documents be encrypted on the client side, and the audit team checks key usage records for the Seoul and Tokyo keys separately in each Region's CloudTrail. Encryption is handled using the envelope method by generating a data key for each object. There are not yet any resources in Tokyo created with this key. Which key configuration is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a multi-Region primary key in Seoul, create a replica key in Tokyo, and set the key policy and grants separately on the key in each Region.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use AWS managed keys in both Seoul and Tokyo, and modify the policy of the Tokyo Region key to match the contents of the Seoul Region policy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Continue to use the single-Region KMS key in Seoul, and have the Tokyo application make cross-Region Decrypt calls to the KMS endpoint in the Seoul Region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a new single-Region KMS key in Tokyo, re-encrypt all ciphertext in Seoul with the Tokyo key, and copy it to a bucket in the Tokyo Region.

explanation: The correct answer is a multi-Region key. Related multi-Region keys share the same key ID and key material, so data encrypted in one Region can be decrypted with the replica key in another Region without re-encryption or cross-Region calls, and key policies and grants are managed independently for each Region. Calling the Seoul key cross-Region makes decryption impossible during a Seoul outage and also conflicts with the prohibition on calling KMS. Creating a new key in Tokyo would require re-encrypting all data, which violates the constraints. AWS managed keys are always single-Region keys, so they cannot share key material across Regions, and their policies cannot be modified.

prompt: A company must record management events from all accounts in the organization in a single Amazon S3 bucket in a central log archive account. Newly created accounts must also be included automatically, and administrators of member accounts must not be able to stop or modify the trail. The company has a separate log archive account, and the audit team must also be able to verify the integrity of the log files. Dozens of accounts are added every month. Some existing accounts have trails that teams created themselves, but the company intends to consolidate to a single central bucket going forward. Logs must be retained for 7 years, and only the security team can modify the bucket policy in the log archive account. The security team has 3 members and has no capacity to handle per-account exceptions, and it verifies whether log files have been tampered with by using digests. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to create individual trails with the same settings in all accounts, and add stack instances when a new account is created.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have the trail in each account write to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, and configure log group subscription filters to replicate the logs to the central account.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Forward the AWS CloudTrail events in each account to an event bus in the central account with Amazon EventBridge rules, and configure it to store them in Amazon S3 from there.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the management account or a CloudTrail delegated administrator account, create an organization trail that delivers the events of all member accounts to the central bucket.

explanation: The correct answer is an organization trail. When an organization trail is created once in the management account or a delegated administrator account, it records the events of all member accounts in the organization and of accounts added later, and member accounts can view it but cannot modify or stop it. Individual trails created with StackSets can be stopped or modified by member account administrators. Event bus forwarding is not a trail, so it cannot prevent member accounts from deleting rules, and it adds configuration for cleaning up the delivery targets. Log group replication is also a per-account setting that members can modify.

prompt: A threat intelligence report warned of possible malware infection on the company's EC2 instance i-0abc, but there are no related findings at all in Amazon GuardDuty. The instance is in production, and installing an agent or performance degradation is not allowed. The instance has two attached volumes, and rebooting or stopping it is not allowed under the change approval process. This instance uses two EBS volumes, and GuardDuty is already enabled across the organization. The inspection results must be reported within one day, and only one person has permission to access the instance. The investigation results must be attached to the incident report, and the indicators in the threat intelligence report point to only this one instance. Which method confirms whether the attached EBS volumes contain malware with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Scan the instance with Amazon Inspector, review the software vulnerability findings, and compare them against known malware signatures to determine whether it is infected.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Wait and watch the status for a GuardDuty-initiated scan, which starts automatically when GuardDuty generates a malware-related finding.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start an on-demand scan of GuardDuty Malware Protection for EC2 by using the instance ARN.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use Systems Manager to install an antivirus agent on all instances, schedule a full file system scan, and check for infection.

explanation: The correct answer is an on-demand malware scan. You can start it by providing only the instance ARN even when there are no related GuardDuty findings, it scans the attached EBS volumes without an agent, and it is designed not to affect resource performance. A GuardDuty-initiated scan starts only when a finding that indicates possible malware is generated, so it does not run now when there are no findings. Inspector is a service that finds software vulnerabilities and does not determine malware infection. Installing an antivirus agent violates the constraints that do not allow an agent or performance degradation.

prompt: Under the company's ransomware response policy, no one, including administrator accounts and the root user, may be able to delete the recovery points in an AWS Backup vault during the retention period. However, because mistakes can be made in the retention period settings, it must be possible to cancel or change the configuration for a few days after the lock is applied. The backup targets are Amazon EBS and Amazon RDS, the retention period is 1 year, and no team other than the security team has permission to change vault settings. Backups run every day at dawn, and the recovery points are gathered in one vault in the same Region. The security team considers it sufficient to be able to correct configuration mistakes only within the first few days. The backup resources are 200 EBS volumes and 40 RDS instances, and the recovery points created after the time the vault lock is applied are the ones to be protected. Which configuration is MOST appropriate to meet the requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set the vault access policy to deny the backup:DeleteRecoveryPoint action for all principals, and limit the permission to change the policy to the security team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure the backup plan to copy recovery points to a vault in another account, and operate without applying a separate lock to the source vault.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a vault lock in governance mode, specify the minimum and maximum retention periods, and allow only users with sufficient permissions to remove the lock.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a compliance mode vault lock and specify a changeable period (grace time) of at least 3 days.

explanation: The correct answer is a compliance mode vault lock with a grace period. In compliance mode, after the grace period (minimum 3 days) ends, no one, including the customer, the account owner, or AWS, can change or delete the lock, and during the grace period the lock can be removed or the configuration changed, so configuration mistakes can be corrected. In governance mode, users with sufficient IAM permissions can remove the lock, which does not satisfy the requirement that no one can delete. A vault access policy can be removed by an administrator who can change the policy. Copying without locking leaves the original recovery points vulnerable to deletion.

prompt: 120 developers at a SaaS company start and stop EC2 instances for 40 projects. A project tagging scheme is already applied to all instances, and each developer must be able to work only with instances that have the same Project tag as the project the developer belongs to. A few new projects are created each quarter, and the company wants to operate with a single policy without creating or modifying IAM policies each time. Employee accounts and per-project groups are managed in an external IdP, and users sign in to AWS with IAM Identity Center. The security team has 3 members. A developer belongs to only one project and not to multiple projects at the same time, and when a project ends, removing the developer from the group must be enough to complete the revocation of permissions. Which method is MOST appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create one permission set and IAM policy for each project that lists the ARNs of that project's instances, and assign it to the developer group.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pass the IdP's project value as an attribute for access control in IAM Identity Center, and in the permission set policy, allow EC2 actions only when the Project tag on the resource matches the tag on the principal.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure an organization SCP to deny EC2 actions whose project tags do not match, and grant the PowerUserAccess permission commonly to developers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Attach a resource-based policy to each instance that allows the account IDs of that project's developers, and update the policy when a project is added.

explanation: Attribute-based access control passes IdP attributes as session tags, and a single policy compares whether the aws:PrincipalTag and aws:ResourceTag values are equal, so no policy changes are needed even as projects increase. Per-project policies leave the burden of continually adding to 40 policies. An SCP cannot grant permissions, and even when combined with PowerUserAccess it cannot map the tag comparison to a person's tag. EC2 instances do not have resource-based policies.

prompt: A security analysis SaaS vendor uses a single account ID to call AssumeRole on read-only IAM roles in dozens of customer accounts to inspect their configurations. Customers enter the role ARN for each customer directly in the vendor's service screen. Currently, the trust policy is restricted to only the vendor's AWS account. However, there is a concern about the confused deputy problem: if one customer finds out another customer's role ARN and registers it with the vendor service, the vendor could assume that role on the customer's behalf and display the information. The number of customers keeps growing, so the vendor cannot make major changes to its code, and customers can modify only the trust policies in their own accounts. The vendor can issue and manage a unique identifier for each customer, and customers can copy the value that the vendor provides into the trust policy as is. Which method MOST appropriately reduces this risk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Narrow the principal in the trust policy from the entire vendor account to one specific IAM role ARN used by the vendor, to restrict other principals from assuming it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reduce the role maximum session duration from one hour to 15 minutes to change the setting so that the period in which issued temporary credentials can be abused is shortened.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Put a sts:ExternalId condition that is unique to each customer in the trust policy, and have the vendor pass the per-customer value in the AssumeRole call.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a read-only IAM user in the customer account and hand the access keys to the vendor so that the vendor calls directly without assuming a role.

explanation: The external ID condition makes the role assumable only by a caller that knows the unique value that the vendor issued per customer. Therefore, even if another customer registers someone else's role ARN, the vendor's call that uses that customer's external ID is denied, which prevents the confused deputy problem. The value must be generated and controlled by the vendor for each customer, not by the customer. Narrowing to one specific vendor role still leaves confusion among customers because the vendor calls all customers with the same role. Reducing the session duration only shortens the period of abuse after issuance and does not block the cause. Long-term access keys increase the risk further.

prompt: The security team used Amazon GuardDuty to confirm signs that an attacker has already opened an SSH session on an EC2 instance in a public subnet and is communicating with an external C2 server. The instance security group allows inbound port 22 only from a specific administrator IP range and allows only some ports outbound. There is only this one instance in the subnet, and the instance must remain running because of the memory evidence. The credentials the attacker used on the instance have already been disabled, but the forensics team must acquire memory from the running instance within one hour. The instance role is not used by other services. This instance is directly accessible through its public IP, and there are currently no other instances using the same subnet. The subnet's network ACL uses the default settings (allow all traffic). Which isolation method is MOST appropriate to immediately cut off connections that are already established while preserving evidence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add deny rules for all inbound and outbound traffic to the subnet network ACL at the highest priority, and also apply an isolation security group.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replace the instance's security group with a dedicated isolation security group that has empty inbound and outbound rules, and wait for the existing connections to be dropped.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Stop the instance, then create snapshots of the attached EBS volumes and share them with the analysis account to make sure that the attacker's access is cut off.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Terminate the instance, launch a new instance from a clean golden AMI, and detach only the compromised instance's EBS volumes to keep as evidence.

explanation: The correct answer is to add deny rules to the subnet network ACL. Security groups use connection tracking, so even if you change or remove the rules, connections that are already tracked remain allowed until they time out, but block rules in a stateless network ACL also cut existing connections. There is only one instance in the subnet, so other workloads are not affected. Replacing the group with an empty security group alone may leave the SSH and C2 sessions in place, so it does not satisfy the requirement for immediate blocking. Stopping the instance causes the memory evidence to be lost, which violates the constraint to keep it running. Terminating and relaunching destroys both the volatile evidence and the running state.

prompt: A company that manages employee accounts and department groups in its on-premises identity provider wants employees to sign in to the AWS Management Console through its on-premises SAML 2.0 IdP. Employees must be able to choose different AWS roles depending on their department when they sign in, and the company has decided not to create separate IAM users on the AWS side. There are about 800 employees, and the IdP can already include department information in the SAML assertion. Two members of the infrastructure team will handle the federation work. The federation configuration on the AWS side is managed as IaC, and when the temporary credentials expire after an employee signs in, the employee signs in again through the IdP. The company plans to create 8 roles in total, one per department. Which TWO items must be configured for this federation to work? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure the IdP to include the Role and RoleSessionName attributes in the SAML response to pass the role ARN to assume and the provider ARN.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an IAM SAML identity provider from the IdP's SAML metadata, and create IAM roles with a trust policy that allows sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create roles with a trust policy that allows sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, and have the IdP submit OIDC ID tokens directly to AWS.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an IAM user for each employee, name it the same as the IdP account name, and pass the console password in the SAML response.

choices.label: E
choices.text: In the IAM role trust policy, add the public IP address of the IdP server as an aws:SourceIp condition so that only requests from that IP can assume the role.

explanation: SAML federation requires an IAM SAML provider created from the IdP metadata and roles that trust that provider and allow AssumeRoleWithSAML, and the IdP must include the Role and RoleSessionName attributes in the SAML response to indicate which role to assume. There is no need to create IAM users for each employee, and passwords are not placed in the SAML response. AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity is used for OIDC-based federation, so it does not fit SAML. An IdP server IP condition does not match the request path of the user's browser and is not a required setting.

prompt: An online bookstore's login page receives millions of requests per day, and many enterprise customers connect from behind their corporate NAT. An AWS WAF web ACL is associated with the ALB. Recently, password brute-force attacks against the /login path have continued, and the company wants to block a client IP when it exceeds 100 requests in 5 minutes. However, enterprise customers behind the same NAT legitimately call paths other than /login thousands of times every 5 minutes, so they must not be blocked. The rule must be managed in the web ACL without a code deployment. The rule will be applied directly as Block without first being tested in Count, and the evaluation window will use 5 minutes from the values that WAF supports. Which rule will meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a rate-based rule that aggregates by IP with a 5-minute evaluation window and a limit of 100, and use a scope-down statement so that only requests whose URI path is /login are counted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an IP-aggregated rate-based rule with a limit of 100 requests per 5 minutes without a scope-down, so that requests on all paths of the web ACL are counted against the same limit.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add the AWS WAF Bot Control targeted-protection-level managed rule group to the web ACL to automatically distinguish and block brute-force attacks on login requests.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set a request rate limit value in the ALB security group inbound rules to deny connection attempts of 100 or more per 5 minutes per client IP.

explanation: A rate-based rule counts the requests within the evaluation window for each aggregation key such as IP, and by using a scope-down statement it can track only requests to the /login path and apply the limit, so normal calls to other paths are not affected. Without a scope-down, all calls from users behind the NAT are counted against the same IP limit and are blocked. Bot Control incurs additional charges and is excessive compared with the simple limit rule that was requested. Security groups do not have a request rate limiting feature.

prompt: A company introduced a security requirement to turn on EBS encryption by default. The administrator enabled default encryption only in the Seoul Region, and a subsequent audit found that new unencrypted volumes had been created in the Virginia Region and that some existing volumes in Seoul are also not encrypted. There are hundreds of target volumes in each Region, and all changes are made through a planned procedure. The short downtime needed to replace volumes is allowed during the scheduled maintenance window, but data loss is not allowed. The volumes to be replaced include a mix of databases and file servers, so the mount points differ by volume, and each new volume must be created in the same Availability Zone as the existing volume. The tags and snapshot metadata before and after the replacement must be retained for cost tracking. Which TWO actions are MOST appropriate to resolve both problems? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use ModifyVolume to turn on the encryption attribute of the volume and encrypt the existing volume in place.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable EBS encryption by default in every other Region where workloads run.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a snapshot of each unencrypted volume, copy it with the encryption option, create a new volume from that snapshot, and replace the existing volume.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the default key setting in the Seoul Region by switching the default encryption KMS key to a customer managed key, so that existing volumes are re-encrypted with the new key.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Only recheck the setting status in the Regions that were flagged, because the Seoul default encryption setting is automatically propagated to all Regions in the account.

explanation: The correct answers are to turn on default encryption in the other Regions and to replace existing volumes with encrypted snapshot copies. Default encryption is a per-Region setting, so it must be turned on in each Region, and it does not affect existing volumes and snapshots, so existing volumes are converted by encrypting the snapshot while copying it and creating a new volume. The statement that the Seoul setting propagates to other Regions is wrong. ModifyVolume has no capability to turn on encryption for an existing volume. Changing the default key affects only volumes created in the future and does not re-encrypt existing volumes.

prompt: An external auditor requires SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification reports for the physical security of AWS data centers and for AWS infrastructure. What is requested is AWS's own compliance documentation, not evidence of the configuration of the company's workloads, and the responsible person wants to download it directly from the account and submit it. The audit deadline is tight, so the company wants to obtain the documents directly from the account without going through a separate request process. The company has already collected configuration evidence for its own accounts with AWS Config and AWS Security Hub CSPM, and the auditor received that as separate evidence. The responsible person must obtain the documents by the day before the audit starts. The requested items are the SOC 2 Type II report and the ISO 27001 certificate, and the responsible person already has permission to sign in to the account. Which service will meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Evaluate the compliance status of the company's resources with an AWS Config conformance pack, and submit the score and the list of noncompliant resources as a report.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an assessment in AWS Audit Manager to automatically collect evidence about the company's AWS usage, generate a report, and submit it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Download the AWS infrastructure compliance reports and certificates on demand from AWS Artifact and submit them to the auditor.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Export the security standard check results from AWS Security Hub and submit the per-account control pass rates to the auditor as evidence.

explanation: The correct answer is AWS Artifact. Artifact is a self-service portal where you can download directly from your account the certificates and reports that show that AWS infrastructure meets compliance requirements. Audit Manager is a service that collects evidence showing whether the company's AWS usage complies with regulations, so it is not AWS's own certification documentation. An AWS Config conformance pack evaluates the configuration compliance of the company's resources. Security Hub only shows the results of security standard checks for the account and does not provide AWS's own certification reports.

prompt: A manufacturing company that manages the accounts of its 800 employees in Microsoft Entra ID wants to consolidate access to its 60 AWS accounts with AWS IAM Identity Center. Hires, departures, and department transfers occur every week, and the HR team enters changes only in Entra ID. The security team wants a departing employee's AWS access to be removed within one day. Permission sets are assigned to accounts at the department group level. The company does not want a procedure for creating and deleting users manually on the AWS side, and the cloud team has 2 members and cannot build and operate a separate synchronization program. The Entra ID group names are the same as the department names, and the AWS accounts belong to a single organization. Currently, IAM users exist in each account, and the company is phasing them out. Which configuration meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Connect Entra ID only as a SAML provider and bulk import users into Identity Center from a CSV file, with the responsible person re-importing whenever there are changes such as hires or departures.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Connect Entra ID as the external identity provider for IAM Identity Center, synchronize users and groups with SCIM automatic provisioning, and assign permission sets to the groups.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Register an IAM SAML provider in each of the 60 accounts, create an IAM role for each department, and have the Entra ID app pass the per-account role attributes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create users directly in the Identity Center directory, and operate a procedure in which the responsible person receives an HR team request email and deletes the user when someone leaves.

explanation: Identity Center automatically synchronizes users and groups with an external identity provider through SCIM, so hires, departures, and transfers are reflected on the AWS side without manual work, and assigning permission sets to the synchronized groups consolidates per-account access. Connecting only SAML and importing a CSV requires periodic manual handling of the user lifecycle. Per-account SAML providers and roles increase the configuration across 60 accounts and run counter to the goal of centralization. Creating and deleting users directly is in direct conflict with the requirement.

prompt: A security lead in an organization attached an SCP that denies all ec2:* actions to the organization root, and the default FullAWSAccess policy remains in place. The organization has a management account, a member account that acts as the delegated administrator for security services, and dozens of general workload member accounts. This SCP is attached to the organization root, so it applies normally to all member accounts. Afterward, the team found cases in which EC2-related calls still succeed in accounts that should not be using EC2, and is investigating the cause. The principle is that the management account is used only for organization management tasks, but some administrators sometimes sign in directly and use it when in a hurry. A few accounts still have workloads that use load balancers. Considering the scope of SCP application, which TWO cases are the most accurate in which EC2-related calls still succeed? (Select TWO.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A call by an administrator role in the member account designated as the delegated administrator to launch an instance

choices.label: B
choices.text: A call by the Elastic Load Balancing service-linked role in a member account to create a network interface for a load balancer

choices.label: C
choices.text: A call by an IAM role with the AdministratorAccess policy attached in a member account to launch an instance

choices.label: D
choices.text: A call by the root user of a member account to launch an instance with ec2:RunInstances

choices.label: E
choices.text: A call by an administrator role that has ec2:RunInstances permission in the management account to launch an instance

explanation: The correct answers are a call from the management account and a call by a service-linked role. SCPs do not affect the users and roles of the management account, and they cannot restrict actions performed by service-linked roles. The root user of a member account is subject to SCPs, so the call is denied. A member account role with AdministratorAccess also fails because the SCP deny takes precedence. A member account designated as a delegated administrator is also subject to the SCP as is, so the call is blocked. Therefore, only the management account and the service-linked role cases succeed.

prompt: A healthcare data company has received an audit requirement that, under regulations, data must be accessed only over private paths and that requests that pass through a NAT gateway are not allowed. The data bucket must be accessed only from workloads in the VPC vpc-0a1, and traffic must come only through an S3 gateway endpoint. The team allowed the VPC CIDR 10.0.0.0/16 with aws:SourceIp in the bucket policy, but all requests were denied. The workload instances are in private subnets, and the gateway endpoint is already associated with the route table. There is one bucket, and the changes must stay within the scope of the policy and the endpoint. The audit team prefers using a deny condition in the policy rather than an allow condition, and administrator console access has already been separated to a different path for this bucket. Which fix will meet the requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add the VPC's NAT gateway Elastic IP address to the aws:SourceIp condition of the bucket policy, so that requests leaving through the internet path are also included in the same allowed range.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove the aws:SourceIp condition from the bucket policy and change it to deny requests where aws:SourceVpce does not match the ID of that gateway endpoint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Attach an endpoint policy to the gateway endpoint that allows only that bucket, and keep only the block public access setting in the bucket policy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Associate a security group with the gateway endpoint that allows only port 443 from the VPC CIDR, and leave the IP condition in the bucket policy as it is.

explanation: The aws:SourceIp key is not included in the request context for requests that go through a gateway endpoint, so allowing the VPC CIDR with this condition results in everything being denied. To allow only endpoint-based access, use an aws:SourceVpce condition in the bucket policy to deny requests that do not come from the specific endpoint. Allowing the NAT Elastic IP would open an internet path that is not the endpoint and violates the requirement. An endpoint policy only restricts requests leaving the VPC and is not a means for the bucket to block external access. A security group cannot be associated with a gateway endpoint.

prompt: A financial company has only 3 incident response staff, and the time available for an investigation is within 1 hour per case. Today, GuardDuty produced a finding that the credentials of an EC2 instance role in a production account were used from an external IP. The analyst must check, in a single-screen workflow, without building a separate log pipeline or query tables, how much the role's API call volume and the connecting IPs and geolocations differ from the usual pattern, and what the related instances and IPs are. Time is short to determine the scope of the investigation and include it in the incident report. CloudTrail and VPC flow logs are already enabled in all accounts, but no query environment for analysis has been configured. The responsible analyst is using the relevant service for the first time. What should be used to perform this scoping investigation with the LEAST effort?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Collect the CloudTrail logs and VPC flow logs in Amazon S3, create Amazon Athena tables, and directly aggregate call statistics per role ARN and IP with SQL.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create an AWS Security Hub CSPM insight to gather the findings associated with the role, and compare the historical call volume trend on the insight screen.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Scan the buckets the role accessed with Amazon Macie, and trace back records to determine what sensitive data was sent to which IP.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pivot from the GuardDuty finding to Amazon Detective, and compare against the normal pattern by using the entity profiles and behavior graph visualizations for the role and the IP.

explanation: Detective automatically ingests CloudTrail, VPC flow logs, GuardDuty findings, and more to build a behavior graph. From a GuardDuty finding, you can go directly to an entity profile such as a role or IP, compare call volume and connecting geolocation against the usual pattern, and follow related entities. Athena aggregation requires you to build the log tables and queries yourself, which takes a lot of effort. Security Hub CSPM insights only group and display findings and do not provide behavioral baseline comparison. Macie is for detecting sensitive data in S3 and is not a tool for investigating the scope of credential misuse.

prompt: A medical records archive system must ensure that all objects in an Amazon S3 bucket cannot be deleted or overwritten by anyone, including the root user, for 7 years. In addition, because of litigation, some objects must not be deleted even after 7 years, for a period whose end point is unknown, and only the legal team must be able to release them. Versioning is already turned on for the bucket, and there are tens of millions of objects. Some patient records may receive deletion requests before the retention period ends, but under regulations the retention period takes precedence. The security team wants to avoid the work of managing a retention period separately for each object. The legal team organizes the list of objects subject to litigation by case number and delivers it, and the targets change frequently. The auditor wants a history of changes to retention settings to remain. Which configuration will meet these requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set the Object Lock default retention to governance mode for 7 years, and give only the legal team role the s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission so that it manages retention during litigation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the Object Lock default retention to compliance mode for 30 years, locking all objects for a long period so that retention is never released before the litigation ends.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Turn on MFA delete for the bucket and deny s3:DeleteObjectVersion to all principals in the bucket policy to prevent deletion during the retention period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set the Object Lock default retention to compliance mode for 7 years, apply legal holds to the objects subject to litigation, and grant the legal hold permission only to the legal team.

explanation: The correct answer is the combination of compliance mode default retention and legal holds. Compliance mode prevents anyone, including the root user, from deleting or overwriting an object version within the retention period, and a legal hold has no expiration date and remains until it is explicitly released, and only users with the s3:PutObjectLegalHold permission can set or release it. Governance mode lets users with the bypass permission change retention or delete, which violates the requirement that not even root can do so. A 30-year compliance retention cannot be shortened and is excessive for all objects. MFA delete and a bucket policy can be removed by an administrator who can modify them, so they are not immutable.

prompt: In a company that uses two accounts in the same organization, the CI pipeline in account A tries to assume the deploy role in account B at every deployment but gets AccessDenied (no sts:AssumeRole permission). The trust policy of the deploy role in account B lists the account A root as the principal, and the CI role in account A has only an S3 access policy attached. Today's deployment is blocked and the release is delayed, and there is no time to touch organization-wide policies or the configuration of other accounts. The CI role is used only for the pipeline in account A, and account B has already reviewed and approved the permissions policy of the deploy role. The two accounts are in the same OU in Organizations, and only the default FullAWSAccess SCP is applied. Which method is MOST appropriate to resolve this with minimal changes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the principal in the trust policy of the deploy role in account B from the account A root to the ARN of the account A CI role, to narrow the trust scope.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attach a permissions boundary to the deploy role in account B and include a statement that allows sts:AssumeRole in the boundary policy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add an allow for sts:AssumeRole on the ARN of the deploy role in account B to the identity-based policy of the CI role in account A.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add an sts:AssumeRole allow statement to the SCP of the OU that account A belongs to so that all accounts can assume each other's roles.

explanation: Cross-account role assumption must be allowed both in the trust policy of the target account and in the identity-based policy of the calling principal in the caller's account. The trust policy already allows account A, so what is missing is the sts:AssumeRole permission on the CI role. Narrowing the trust principal to the CI role is a more restrictive change and does not resolve the missing permission on the calling side. A permissions boundary does not grant permissions and only restricts them. An SCP also cannot grant permissions with an allow statement.

prompt: An organization operates 80 accounts with AWS Organizations, and dozens of new accounts are created each month. The security team wants GuardDuty to be turned on in both the Seoul and Tokyo Regions for both existing accounts and accounts that will be created in the future. The team does not want to use management account credentials for day-to-day security operations, and wants to avoid having a responsible person enable it account by account or building and operating separate automation each time an account is created. Accounts are created directly with the Organizations API without using Control Tower, and new accounts must be protected by GuardDuty within the same day after creation. The security team has 3 members. The team wants to eliminate the procedure of making a request to a responsible person each time an account is created. Which method has the LEAST operational overhead?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Designate a dedicated security member account as the GuardDuty delegated administrator, and from that account set organization auto-enable to all accounts (ALL) in each of the Seoul and Tokyo Regions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Designate a dedicated security member account as the GuardDuty delegated administrator, and from that account set organization auto-enable to new accounts only (NEW) in each of the Seoul and Tokyo Regions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receive the account creation event of the management account with an Amazon EventBridge rule, and implement an AWS Lambda function that enables GuardDuty in both Regions of the new account.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Document a procedure for signing in to each member account and enabling GuardDuty in both Regions in the console, and have the responsible person repeat it each time an account is created.

explanation: The correct answer is a delegated administrator with organization auto-enable (ALL). When the management account designates the security account as the delegated administrator, that account manages the organization's member accounts, and setting auto-enable to ALL turns on GuardDuty for both existing accounts and newly joining accounts. GuardDuty is a Regional service, so it must be configured separately in Seoul and Tokyo. NEW applies only to new accounts, so the 80 existing accounts would be missed. An event plus Lambda implementation carries the burden of building and maintaining code. Manual per-account enablement results in omissions and repetition as accounts grow.

prompt: Application code calls AWS Secrets Manager by using the default name secretsmanager.ap-northeast-2.amazonaws.com, and the code cannot be changed. The company is creating an interface endpoint so that dozens of servers in private subnets can use this service without an internet path, but when the option to enable the private DNS name is selected, enabling fails because of the VPC settings. DNS resolution is turned on and DNS hostnames is turned off for this VPC. The endpoint security group already allows port 443 from the entire VPC. The VPC spans multiple subnets and Availability Zones, and the servers that use the same endpoint are replaced with new ones at every deployment. The application settings are fixed in the server image, so a deployment that changes the call address is not allowed. What should be done to resolve this with the fewest settings and without code changes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the call URL in the application settings to the endpoint-specific DNS name, and apply it to all servers through the deployment pipeline.

choices.label: B
